---
title: Command line
---

The `dazflow` command runs a project folder: the same steps, configuration
and outputs as `dz.project.load(...).run()` and `.write()`. It is installed
with the package; `python -m dazflow` works too. Every output below is
pasted from a real run.

```sh
$ dazflow --help
 Usage: dazflow [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

 A time-series modelling workflow whose every step returns documented artefacts.

╭─ Commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ init      Create a project folder with commented defaults and example data.          │
│ validate  Check the configuration and that every input reads, without running a      │
│           step.                                                                      │
│ run       Run the pipeline's steps in order; stop after a step whose gate fails      │
│           (exit 2).                                                                  │
│ replay    Rerun every step from reports/record.json and compare; exit 2 on a         │
│           difference.                                                                │
│ show      Print one table or finding of the last run (a figure: its file).           │
│ plugins   List the registered components of every kind, built in and from plugins.   │
│ build     Run the build step on the project, from the last run's earlier results;    │
│           write reports/build/.                                                      │
  ...
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Every command but `init` works on the project in the current folder, or the
one `-p/--project` names.

## A project

`dazflow init` writes a project folder: `project.yaml`, one commented file
per step under `config/` with every setting at its default, and example
data. `validate` reads the configuration and every input without running a
step.

```sh
$ dazflow init loss-rate
created loss-rate (11 files); next: dazflow validate -p loss-rate
$ cd loss-rate
$ dazflow validate
loss-rate: valid; steps ingest, clean, explore, build, select, forecast, diagnose, report; 2 inputs read
```

## Running steps

`dazflow run` runs the pipeline in order and writes each step's tables,
figures and finding to `reports/<step>/`, its dataset to `data/`, and the
run record to `reports/record.json`. `--to` stops after a step:

```sh
$ dazflow run --to explore
ingest: gate passed; 4 artefacts in reports/ingest/
  3 of 3 configured series were found and put on a quarterly calendar from 1995Q1 to 2024Q4. The targets and drivers overlap on 120 quarters, against a minimum of 40.
clean: gate passed; 5 artefacts in reports/clean/
  7 checks on 3 series flagged 1 periods before treatment. 0 treatments changed 0 values. After treatment, 0 of 12 checks fail.
explore: gate passed; 6 artefacts in reports/explore/
  3 series explored; 2 were differenced to stationarity. 2 of 2 drivers are kept, 0 of them by override: each has its expected sign and a p-value of at most 0.05.
```

`--from` carries the earlier steps from the last record, their datasets
read back and checked against the recorded fingerprints, and runs the rest:

```sh
$ dazflow run --from build
build: gate passed; 6 artefacts in reports/build/
  3 candidates were fitted on 3 driver combinations of up to 2 drivers, beside 2 benchmarks; 3 pass every check: each driver has its expected sign and a p-value of at most 0.05, and no VIF exceeds 10.00.
select: gate passed; 8 artefacts in reports/select/
  5 models were scored at 60 origins, their errors scaled by the mean benchmark's; the model confidence set at 0.10 holds 1 of them, 1 passing every check. ols:gdp_growth+unemployment is proposed: 2 drivers and a scaled error of 0.39.
  ...
report: gate passed; 6 artefacts in reports/report/
  The document reports 7 steps, ingest to diagnose, in pipeline order, with 26 tables, 10 figures and 7 findings. Every step's gate passed, 1 check by override with a reason.
```

Each step is also a command of its own: `dazflow select` is
`dazflow run --from select --to select`. A step from a plugin gets its
command the same way.

## Reading the results

`dazflow show` prints one table or finding of the last run by its
identifier, or the path of a figure. Tables and findings are written in the
project's style, as in `reports/<step>/`:

```sh
$ dazflow show T6.1
Table T6.1. Ranking of the candidates

| Rank | Candidate | Role | Drivers | Scaled error | In the confidence set | MCS p-value | Build checks | Beats the benchmark | Scenarios out of order | Projections out of bounds | Choice | Passes every check |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | ---: | :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | ols:gdp\_growth+unemployment | candidate | 2 | 0.39 | yes | 1.00 | pass | yes | 0 | 0 | chosen | Pass |
| 2 | ols:unemployment | candidate | 1 | 0.49 | no | 0.01 | pass | yes | 0 | 0 |  | Pass |
| 3 | ols:gdp\_growth | candidate | 1 | 0.54 | no | 0.01 | pass | yes | 0 | 0 |  | Pass |
| 4 | mean | benchmark | 0 | 1.00 | no | 0.00 | pass | no | 0 | 0 |  | **Fail** |
| 5 | naive | benchmark | 0 | 1.27 | no | 0.00 | pass | no | 0 | 0 |  | **Fail** |

Scaled error: the candidate's rolling-origin RMSE over the mean benchmark's; it beats the benchmark below 1.
$ dazflow show S6.1
5 models were scored at 60 origins, their errors scaled by the mean benchmark's; the model confidence set at 0.10 holds 1 of them, 1 passing every check. ols:gdp_growth+unemployment is proposed: 2 drivers and a scaled error of 0.39.
$ dazflow show F3.1
F3.1: Lag profiles: correlation of each driver with loss_rate, by lag
reports/explore/F3.1.svg
```

`--json` on `run`, `validate`, `show`, `replay` and `plugins` prints the
result as JSON instead; for `run` it is the run record.

## Gates and exit status

`0` when every gate passed, `1` on an error (its message, what was observed
and what to change go to stderr), `2` when a gate failed. A failed gate
stops the run after that step, which is still written, with the record's
status `gate_failed`. The example's RESET test fails and is accepted by an
override in `config/diagnose.yaml`; with the override removed:

```sh
$ dazflow run --from diagnose
diagnose: gate FAILED (reset); 9 artefacts in reports/diagnose/
  ols:gdp_growth+unemployment passes 11 of 12 diagnostic checks and fails reset. Back-tested from 57 origins up to 4 periods ahead, its 95% interval covered 0.96 of the actual values, and 1 of 119 observations lie outside its 99% interval.
stopped after diagnose: its gate failed
$ echo $?
2
```

An error names what it found and what to change:

```sh
$ dazflow validate
error: the IngestConfig YAML does not parse
  observed: duplicate key 'frequency'   in "<unicode string>", line 48, column 1:     frequency: X     ^
  change: Correct the YAML syntax at the position given.
$ echo $?
1
```

## Report and replay

The `report` step, last in the default pipeline, writes the Word document
and a replay script to `reports/document/`. `dazflow replay` reruns every
step from the record and compares each recorded number with what it
computes now (floats within a relative 1e-9, the rest exactly), and also
checks that `project.yaml` and `config/` still equal the recorded
configuration. It exits `0` on a match and `2` on a difference; the script
does the same without the command line.

```sh
$ dazflow report
report: gate passed; 6 artefacts in reports/report/
  The document reports 7 steps, ingest to diagnose, in pipeline order, with 26 tables, 10 figures and 7 findings. Every step's gate passed, 1 check by override with a reason.
$ dazflow replay
replay of run 20261126T005350Z-ff9f2976 (8 steps rerun): matches its record (rtol 1e-09, atol 1e-12)
$ python reports/document/replay.py
replay of run 20261126T005350Z-ff9f2976 (8 steps rerun): matches its record (rtol 1e-09, atol 1e-12)
```

## Plugins

`dazflow plugins` lists the registered components by kind, built in and
from installed plugins (see [Writing a plugin](writing-a-plugin.qmd)):

```sh
$ dazflow plugins
step: build, clean, diagnose, explore, forecast, ingest, report, select
step adapter: build, clean, diagnose, forecast, ingest, report, select
reader: csv, excel, parquet
check: completeness, duplicates, gaps, outliers, range, representativeness, revisions
transform: boxcox, diff, growth, log, logdiff, logit, seasonal_diff
renderer: docx, html, markdown, png, svg
```
